Whistleblower David Grusch joins Joe Rogan to talk about early UFO recoveries in a segment from the show. Grusch is the former intelligence officer who told Congress that the US holds craft and remains from non-human sources. His claims shook the field.

Grusch tells what he learned of the first finds and how far back the secret runs, as he states it. Rogan asks how he can be sure of tales he heard but did not see. The segment is a tight cut from their talks. Listeners get the core of the most famed UFO claim of the age. The library holds the file as an archive record.

Former Illinois governor Rod Blagojevich joins Tucker Carlson with a prison story Carlson calls hard to believe. Blagojevich jokes that the studio sits far from his old inmate number. He is now writing a book about his fall.

He traces the case back to President Obama and a Senate seat deal. He later won release through help tied to President Trump. The title accuses Kamala Harris of corruption. Blagojevich also names what he sees as the true cause of his party's slide. The episode is part memoir and part payback.

Part four of Tucker Carlson's series The 9/11 Files looks at how doubt about the attacks grew into a full charge of conspiracy. The episode title names the shift from cover-up to conspiracy. Carlson guides the series in his own voice.

The episode walks through the gaps in the known story that fed public doubt over the years. It names the claims that moved from fringe talk to wide debate. Carlson argues the state hid facts, and that the hiding bred the wildest claims. Listeners get one part of a longer case. The library keeps the series as an archive record, without taking a side on its claims.
